Personal take: Most XR developers are still underestimating how big Meta VR Glasses could be for the industry.
Not because the hardware is perfect right now, but because the form factor removes one of the biggest barriers that has held VR back for years.
If experiences can work well on both Quest and Glasses with the same core interactions, the potential audience gets a lot bigger.
Do you think Glasses will actually move the needle for indie developers in the next 18 months, or is it still too early?

item.title: I honestly can’t imagine doing anything else.
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
I honestly can’t imagine doing anything else. I really love XR, and here’s why!
There’s something magical about building an experience that goes beyond a screen and becomes part of the world around you.
What blows my mind even more is taking a game that originally ran on a 2D screen and bringing it into Mixed Reality!
I’ve now converted several of my small iOS games into fully playable MR experiences, and honestly, it’s crazy how different they feel when you can interact with them in your own environment.
After all these years of developing VR/MR games and teaching XR development on YouTube, I still get excited every time I put on a headset and interact with something I created.
That feeling never goes away, and I honestly believe we’re just scratching the surface of what’s possible!

item.title: To be honest, when I first started working at Meta, it was very challenging.

To be honest, when I first started working at Meta, it was very challenging. But like any new job, I knew I had to keep pushing, learning, helping across the organization, and doing what I do best: creating content and educating developers.
Nowadays, it feels like home. I’ve gotten used to the work, but it’s still very challenging, and that’s what keeps me excited!
I also love that I’m building more than ever. It’s not just meetings. I actually get to spend a lot of time building things and sharing what I learn, both internally and externally.

item.title: All, here’s a Unity VR tip worth checking out!
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
All, here’s a Unity VR tip worth checking out!
Have you experimented with Late Latching on Meta Quest?
It updates head and controller tracking poses just before rendering, reducing perceived latency and making VR interactions feel more responsive!
👨🏻‍💻To enable it in Unity: - Use Vulkan + Multiview - Open XR Plug-in Management → OpenXR - Meta Quest Support → Enable Late Latching
One important detail: Late Latching updates rendering poses, not gameplay physics, so be sure to test your interactions on the headset.
You can even measure the improvement using:
adb logcat -s VrApi
Compare the Prd values with Late Latching enabled and disabled to see the difference! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120912928798859353/video/1

item.dc:creator: Dilmerv

Guys, I found another very cool feature for Quest & Meta VR Glasses devs! 👇
OVR Metrics Tool lets you add your own metrics in Unity C# and see them alongside FPS, CPU, and GPU. For Hand Skate, I’d track how many tricks the player lands.
Register the metric once with `DefineAppMetric`, then update it whenever the game confirms a landing.
`OVRMetricsToolSDK.Instance.UpdateAppMetric("tricks_landed", total);`
You can see the counter live in the headset with Metrics HUD or save it to CSV with Metrics Recording in Meta VR Developer Hub. https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120735420891717650/video/1

item.title: Here’s a Unity XR shader tip! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s a Unity XR shader tip! 👇
Does your custom shader work in the Editor but render incorrectly in one eye on the headset?
Check its Single-Pass Instanced rendering support!
Make sure you’re using Unity’s stereo macros, including UNITY_VERTEX_OUTPUT_STEREO and UNITY_INITIALIZE_VERTEX_OUTPUT_STEREO.
A great example is shown in this video! The AI agent identified missing stereo macros in my shader. Even though everything looked correct locally, it wasn’t rendering properly on the headset until those fixes were applied.
A good reminder of why testing on the actual device is so important! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120396165338239472/video/1

item.title: 📣 All, here is another great XR Dev Tip!
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
📣 All, here is another great XR Dev Tip!
I’m adding occlusion to Hand Skate. This concept video compares:
- Static: MRUK wall and ceiling planes are cheaper to draw than dense room meshes
- Dynamic: Meta Depth API for moving objects. Hard edges cost less GPU time, while soft edges look smoother
- Hands: Tracked meshes preserve finger gaps with an extra depth pass
ℹ️ You can use Meta’s Depth API for both static and dynamic occlusion, or combine MRUK room meshes for static surfaces with live depth for moving objects.
The C# component is: EnvironmentDepthManager, under Scripts/EnvironmentDepth in the Meta XR Core SDK (com.meta.xr.sdk.core). Unity 6 OpenXR projects also need the Unity OpenXR Meta package (com.unity.xr.meta-openxr).
In Unity, you can start and stop requesting live depth when mixed reality states change.
depth.enabled = inMR && EnvironmentDepthManager.IsSupported; https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120344565781614941/video/1

item.title: Here’s a VR rendering technique every XR developer should know about! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s a VR rendering technique every XR developer should know about! 👇
Foveated Rendering reduces GPU workload by rendering less detail in your peripheral vision while keeping the important areas sharp.
There are three approaches worth exploring:
• Fixed Foveation: Keeps the center sharp while reducing detail toward the edges. • Eye-Tracked Foveation: Moves the high-detail region wherever your eyes look. • Dynamic Foveation: Adjusts foveation strength based on GPU load.
This is especially interesting for Meta VR Glasses, where eye tracking can help developers optimize rendering without sacrificing detail where players are looking!
In Unity, using Meta XR Core SDK, you can enable fixed and dynamic foveation with:
OVRManager.foveatedRenderingLevel = OVRManager.FoveatedRenderingLevel.High; OVRManager.useDynamicFoveatedRendering = true;
For supported eye-tracking devices:
OVRManager.eyeTrackedFoveatedRenderingSupported OVRManager.eyeTrackedFoveatedRenderingEnabled = true;
Eye-tracked foveation also requires the correct project configuration and eye-tracking permission.
More rendering headroom means more opportunities to create visually impressive VR/MR experiences!
Check out the animation to see how these techniques work! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120192393039184290/video/1

Unity XR devs, when would you choose Meta ISDK over Unity XRI + XR Hands? 👇
Both support many of the same core interactions, including grabbing, poking, rays, and locomotion.
For me, it comes down to the platform, available tools, and how much customization I need.
Unity XRI is great for cross-platform development, while ISDK offers specialized hand interactions and deeper Meta integration.
And remember, ISDK Essentials works with Unity XR Hands too!
💡Curious which one you’re using and why? https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120118049395089869/video/1

item.content:encoded:
Here’s a cool Unity tip for gaze + pinch UI! 👀
With Meta ISDK, the key components are:
• EyeGaze + GazeConecaster • GazeInteractor (rig) • GazeInteractable + ConecastableCanvas • PointableCanvas + GraphicRaycaster • PointableCanvasModule (EventSystem)
💡 Easier setup? Right-click your World Space Canvas → Interaction SDK → Add Gaze Interaction to Canvas.
The wizard configures the required components for you! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2119195793881981396/video/1

Want to get some inspiration from the best of the best when it comes to creating Mixed Reality experiences that feel magical? ✨
Check out this post by Greg Madison, where he shares his work on an experience called “Sphenomenon”! 👇 https://x.com/GregMadison/status/2118404312976273757
引用 @GregMadison：“I’ve never felt such a strong sense of presence in mixed reality.” A sentiment echoed by nearly 100 people who’ve tried Sphenomenon. I built a hands-on playground for creators to feel why the physical world is the ultimate foundation for tomorrow’s augmented interfaces. #astra @OpenAI
